newsitem.title: USA: Clayton Williams cites higher exploration.
newsitem.headline: Clayton Williams cites higher exploration.

text.p: Clayton Williams said Wednesday a decrease in second quarter net income due primarily to higher exploration costs was offset in part by higher oil and gas sales.

On Wednesday, the company reported second quarter net income of $1.2 million, or $0.13 per share, on revenues of $17.1 million, compared to net income of $2.4 million, or $0.32 per share, on revenues of $16.1 million for the same period in 1996.
Discretionary cash flow (net income before exploration costs, depreciation, depletion and amortization and impairments) increased to $11.2 million in 1997 from $9.8 million in 1996.
Clayton expensed $2.4 million of exploration costs during the second quarter of 1997. The company said it utilizes the successful efforts method of accounting.

Oil production was 18 percent higher during the current quarter as compared to the second quarter of 1996 due primarily to strong production performance from wells completed in the northern portion of the North Giddings Block.
The company said it is continuing to evaluate the southern portion of its North Giddings Block and plans to test the Buda and Georgetown formations in that area in August.
Clayton said in response to reduced oil prices and this evaluation it has reduced the number of active rigs in the Giddings area from three to two.
Clayton said it has begun testing infill drilling on the northern portion of its North Giddings Block and believes that some additional locations will be added as a result.
